title: What 18,941 Pest Control Calls Reveal
description: We analyzed 18,941 real calls from homeowners to pest control companies. What separates a call that gets an appointment from one that goes nowhere.
dek: We analyzed 18,941 real calls from homeowners to pest control companies. What separates a call that gets an appointment from one that goes nowhere.
author: Nick Davies
answer: We analyzed 18,941 calls from homeowners to pest control companies between January and July 2026. Across the 7,799 calls where we could identify the pest and see the outcome, 24.6% ended with an appointment being scheduled. The three things that mattered most weren't price or location — they were whether the caller owned the property, whether they could name their pest, and whether the company actually handled that kind of work.

toc.label: Finding 1: Whoever owns the property has to be the one saying yes
Finding 2: Callers who could name the pest did dramatically better
Finding 3: Pest control is far more specialized than most people expect
Finding 4: Which pest you have changes what happens next
Finding 5: With wildlife, the species matters more than the category
Finding 6: Geography matters for which pest, not for whether you get help
Finding 7: Some pests really are seasonal — and some aren't what people think

mainEntity.name: How often do pest control calls actually result in an appointment?

acceptedAnswer.text: In our analysis of 7,799 calls where we could identify the pest and see the outcome, 24.6% ended with an appointment scheduled. Rates varied by pest, from 31.2% for mice and rats down to 19.6% for wildlife. The biggest factors weren't the pest at all — they were whether the caller owned the property and whether they could name what they were dealing with.

mainEntity.name: Why does it matter whether I own my home?

acceptedAnswer.text: Pest treatment requires someone to enter the property and often to do physical work like sealing entry points, which needs the owner's authorization. Confirmed homeowners in our data got appointments 36.0% of the time versus 11.6% when ownership never came up. If you rent, involve your landlord or property manager early rather than calling alone.

mainEntity.name: Do all pest control companies handle all pests?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, and this surprises most homeowners. General work like roaches, ants and rodents is widely available, but bats, termites, bed bugs and wasps are specialist trades. In our data, 19.3% of wildlife callers and roughly 1 in 10 termite, bed bug and wasp callers reached a company that doesn't do that work. Ask before you book.

mainEntity.name: Which pest problems are most likely to need a professional?

acceptedAnswer.text: Structural pests like termites, health-risk pests like bed bugs and rodents, stinging insects near living spaces, and anything that keeps coming back after you've treated it. Within wildlife, animals living in your structure — bats, raccoons, squirrels — lead to a scheduled visit far more often than one-off sightings like a snake in the yard, which frequently needs no visit at all.

Winter, clearly. Mice and rats made up 43.7% of identified pest calls in February, falling to 13.9% by July. This matches published NPMA guidance on rodents seeking indoor shelter in cold months. If you're hearing scratching in walls in late fall, call early — populations grow fast once they're established indoors.

mainEntity.name: Are termites a risk everywhere in the US?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not equally. Termite appointment rates ran 38.8% in the desert Southwest, 32.8% in the Gulf South and Florida, and just 17.6% in cold northern states — a 21-point spread, the widest regional gap we measured for any pest. Termites are a serious structural threat across the southern half of the country and a much smaller concern in the far North.
